Reading film:
# Reading film
## Film language
Film language is the set of techniques filmmakers use to create meaning: mise-en-scène, cinematography, editing and sound.

## The elements
Mise-en-scène covers everything in the frame: setting, costume, lighting, props and performance. Cinematography covers shot size, angle, camera movement and framing. Editing joins shots; continuity editing hides cuts, while montage creates meaning by juxtaposition. Sound can be diegetic, coming from the story world, or non-diegetic, such as a score.

## Key terms
Mise-en-scène: everything placed in the frame
Cinematography: the art of camera work and lighting
Montage: editing that creates meaning by joining contrasting shots
Diegetic sound: sound that comes from the world of the story
Non-diegetic sound: sound added from outside the story world, such as a score
Contextualizing film:
# Contextualizing film
## Context
Films are shaped by their historical, cultural, political, economic and institutional contexts. A film movement is a group of films with shared style and aims, such as German Expressionism, Italian Neorealism or the French New Wave.

## Genre and auteur
A genre is a category with shared conventions, such as horror or the western. Auteur theory sees the director as the author of a film with a recognizable style.

## Key terms
Film movement: a group of films with shared style and aims
Genre: a category of film with shared conventions
Auteur: a director seen as the author of their films
Convention: a typical feature of a genre
Italian Neorealism: a post-war movement using real locations and non-professional actors
Exploring film production roles:
# Exploring film production roles
## Roles
Film production roles include director, screenwriter, cinematographer, editor, sound designer and production designer. Students take on roles and learn how each shapes the film.

## Stages
Production moves through pre-production (script, storyboard, planning), production (filming) and post-production (editing, sound and colour).

## Key terms
Pre-production: planning before filming, including the script and storyboard
Storyboard: a sequence of drawings planning each shot
Post-production: editing, sound and finishing after filming
Cinematographer: the person responsible for camera and lighting
Screenplay: the written script of a film
Textual analysis:
# Textual analysis
## What it is
A written analysis of an extract from a prescribed film, explaining how film elements create meaning in its context.

## Doing it well
Refer to specific moments with timecodes, explain the effect of techniques rather than only naming them, and link them to context.

## Key terms
Extract: a short section of a film
Timecode: a time reference to a moment in a film
Analysis: explaining how techniques create meaning
Effect: the impact of a technique on the audience
Meaning: what a film communicates
Comparative study:
# Comparative study
## What it is
A recorded multimedia comparison of two films from different cultural contexts, focused on a chosen area of film focus.

## Doing it well
Ask a focused question, compare throughout rather than one film then the other, and use clips and sources as evidence.

## Key terms
Comparative study: a comparison of two films from different contexts
Area of film focus: the topic chosen for comparison
Cultural context: the culture in which a film was made
Recorded presentation: a spoken and visual presentation saved as a video
Evidence: clips and sources that support points
Film portfolio:
# Film portfolio
## What it is
A portfolio of filmmaking work in production roles, with reflection on research, choices and outcomes.

## Doing it well
Show research into the role, experiment with techniques, and reflect honestly on what worked and what you would change.

## Key terms
Portfolio: a collection of work with reflection
Production role: a job in making a film
Reflection: thinking critically about choices and outcomes
Experimentation: trying different techniques
Influence: a filmmaker or film that shaped your work
Collaborative film project:
# Collaborative film project
## What it is
At HL students work in a core production team to make an original short film, each taking a production role.

## Doing it well
Plan carefully, communicate as a team, and evaluate both the film and your own contribution.

## Key terms
Collaboration: working together towards a shared goal
Short film: a film of limited running time
Core production team: the small group who make the film
Intention: the effect the filmmakers aim for
Evaluation: judging the success of the film
